literal.prompt: Какой автомобильный протокол связи продвигался для систем by-wire следующего поколения?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: The complete historical Freescale fact sheet states that the FlexRay consortium formed to enable next-generation by-wire systems and promote the automotive protocol (L21-L34), with original adoption history in L35-L52. CAN is the existing general broadcast/control network in the TI context and in the FlexRay comparison L85-L90; INICnet is described as multimedia, while the Ethernet source concerns an automotive physical-layer family. FlexRay is the direct match to this historical promotion purpose among these options. This is not a claim that other networks can never carry by-wire traffic or that FlexRay is the current preferred standard.

absoluteLevel.ground: Identifying FlexRay from its historical advanced by-wire target requires specific automotive-network knowledge beyond ordinary car familiarity. All alternatives are actual in-vehicle networks, so the row is not four random names or grammatically impossible answers. A player with partial knowledge can exclude multimedia-oriented INICnet or distinguish general Ethernet from the dedicated consortium protocol; CAN remains a close control-network distractor. HARD here follows specific knowledge, not an arbitrary requirement for a calculation.
